key_findings.title: FUN_0058CCA0 is CharaElement::vftable[9] - solving the actor-vftable9-investigation pass open question
key_findings.summary: BCS-Y-0528/0529 established that neither the Lua-side Control::Chara/Player/Npc hierarchy nor the engine-side SQEX::CDev::Engine::Fw::SceneObject::Actor::CharaActor hierarchy has a real packet handler at vftable[9] - both have no-ops or scene-graph lifecycle methods at slot 9. The open question 'where ARE the 24 Actor cluster opcodes actually processed?' is now answered: the actor classes whose vftable[9] holds real packet apply methods are the THIRD class hierarchy - Application::Main::Element::* (i.e. RaptureElement and its 27+ subclasses). FUN_0058CCA0 = CharaElement::vftable[9]. FUN_0059CED0 = MapLayoutElement::vftable[9]. FUN_004D8860 = the SHARED slot 9 implementation across 25 OTHER Element subclasses (it appears at vftable+0x24 of RaptureElement, DaemonElement, RelativeElement, XamlElement, FormElement, ClientWorkElement, CustomControlElement, BootupElement, CameraElement, CommonResourceElement, GameManagerElement, ScreenshotManagerElement, CutManagerElement, MainElement, TargetElement, LuaDebugLog, SqwtElement, WidgetElement, EffectElement, EffectDebugElement, DebugWindow, LuaDebugOut, LuaDebugSelect, LightElement, DebugInfoElement). This means the FFXIV 1.x s2c dispatch is partitioned across THREE actor hierarchies: (1) Application::Lua::Script::Client::Control (Lua-side, slot 9 = no-op stub per BCS-Y-0528), (2) Application::Scene::Actor (engine scene-graph, slot 9 = AddReferenceResourceListener per BCS-Y-0529), and (3) Application::Main::Element (the REAL packet-apply hierarchy with 27 distinct slot-9-holding classes routed across 3 implementations including FUN_0058CCA0/FUN_0059CED0/shared FUN_004D8860)
key_findings.invalidates: BCS-Y-0528 'this contradicts the obvious fact that these packets DO have effects' - resolves the contradiction by identifying the third hierarchy
key_findings.implication: Architectural-findings.md client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns' Pattern B needs extension: actor->vftable[9] dispatch routes to Application::Main::Element implementations, NOT to Control:: or SceneActor

key_findings.title: FUN_004D8860 is a SHARED Element::vftable[9] implementation across 25 classes
key_findings.summary: FindAllReferences on FUN_004D8860 reveals 25 distinct data refs to vftable +0x24 slots (in addition to 2 instruction-level CALLs from FUN_0058CCA0 and FUN_0059CED0 as default branches; the 26th data ref at 0x00FAADAC is a Ghidra ref-tracker artifact tracking the FUN_0059CED0 default-branch tail-call). This means FUN_004D8860 is the DEFAULT slot-9 packet handler for 25 different Application::Main::Element subclasses that do NOT have their own override. Per BCS-Y-0280, FUN_004D8860 handles 24 opcode cases via LuaActorImpl vtable trampolines - so these 25 element classes all share the same opcode coverage. CharaElement and MapLayoutElement are the EXCEPTIONS that override slot 9 with class-specific dispatchers (FUN_0058CCA0 and FUN_0059CED0 respectively). The override pattern: their bodies handle class-specific opcodes (Chara-related for CharaElement, Map-related for MapLayoutElement) directly, then fall through to the shared FUN_004D8860 for the common opcode set
key_findings.implication: BCS-Y-0280 should be re-framed as 'Default slot-9 packet apply for the Element hierarchy (25 classes share this implementation)' rather than 'event-family dispatcher'. The 'event family' framing is structurally correct but obscures the polymorphism story

key_findings.title: FUN_0058CCA0 has ZERO instruction-level callers - vtable dispatch confirmed
key_findings.summary: The FUN_0058CCA0-walk pass ran FindReferencesToAddress (instruction-only) and reported refs=1 uniqueCallers=0. The FUN_0058CCA0 caller-tree pass ran FindAllReferences (instruction + data) and confirmed: 0 instruction refs, 1 data ref to CharaElement::vftable +0x24. This validates the Pattern D + Receiver Apply hypothesis: FUN_0058CCA0 is reached ONLY via vtable dispatch. The 'caller list' in the task spec is therefore vacuous in the traditional sense - the caller chain must be reconstructed from the data-ref vtable owner and its dispatcher pattern (which the FUN_0058CCA0 caller-tree pass has done)
key_findings.implication: Later work-up walks on vtable-resident handlers must use FindAllReferences.java, NOT FindReferencesToAddress.java. The latter misses ALL vtable-stored function pointers
